cands.name: Jim Toomey

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Retired businessman with a forty-year career in computer science and information management. He was Chief Information Officer at Loyal American Life Insurance in Mobile and a Divisional Vice President and CIO at Protective Life in Birmingham. Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 47 in 2018, 2022 and 2026.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Jim Toomey holding elected office, so there are no votes or legislative actions to report. His stated positions come mainly from a 2018 Ballotpedia survey and are general: he supported Medicaid expansion, more public education and pre-K funding, anti-corruption measures, and protecting Alabama's natural resources. None of these addresses data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth limits, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice specifically. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 surveys. We found no statements from him on data centers or development, and no documented controversies or foreign ties. The only endorsements we found were recommendations from informal online voter-guide groups, which we did not treat as notable. We could not determine his birth city or when he moved from Mobile to the Birmingham area.

cands.name: Mike Shaw

top: Alabama Credit Union Legislative Action Council
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state representative for Alabama House District 47 (Hoover and Vestavia Hills) since November 2022. Chief technology officer of Mutual Savings Credit Union. Served on the Hoover City Council from 2016 until joining the Legislature. Auburn public administration graduate.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Mike Shaw was born or when he first came to Alabama. The pages we could read did not show his bill sponsorships or actions in office from official records. The bills he lists on his campaign site (such as HB527, HB647, HB82, HB207, HB351 and HB259) rest on his own description only. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or vouchers and charter schools. His site mentions teacher support and education funding, but nothing specific enough to compare with a school-choice or teacher-pay proposal. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him this cycle. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.
